answer: Sybil resistance can be keyed to elapsed time, not capital. Registration must finish a sequential hash chain that cannot be parallelized, checkpointed against a beacon at unpredictable minutes, so one identity costs wall-clock hours whatever a farm's core count. An epoch cap on new keys forces clones into one queue, a summit idle hardware cannot reach faster than one machine. Shortcut chains surface as hollow proofs, checkpoints failing beacon replay, and are dropped. Arrival stamps go into an append-only ledger layered like shale: backdating a chain means rewriting every layer above it.
